title: Declare policy fingerprints and audit canonicalizer for tenant anchoring
author: Priya Shah
description: Problem: RBAC v2 policy rollouts and subsequent policy drift are currently hard to correlate with historical audit records. Multiple teams asked for an auditable, tamper-evident way to bind served access decisions to the exact policy that produced them. This PR introduces two related pieces: 1) a deterministic policy fingerprint (hash + stable normalization) computed at policy compile time and embedded in the policy bundle metadata; 2) an audit canonicalizer that enriches and normalizes audit events with that fingerprint plus compact KMS key metadata (provider, region, key-id-hash) to make retention/forensics queries precise. Motivation: enable post-hoc verification that a given allowed/denied event was evaluated against the same policy snapshot operators expect, and reduce false-positive drift alerts during policy rollouts. Changes: - Add policy fingerprint generator and validator in the RBAC compiler pipeline. Fingerprints are computed using canonical JSON (stable key ordering, type coercion rules) and SHA-256, base64-url encoded. - Embed fingerprint into policy bundle manifest and service discovery so runtime decision caches and authorizers include the fingerprint in decision traces. - Add audit canonicalizer service that: normalizes timestamp formats to RFC3339-UTC, ensures stable header keys (x-rw-audit-...), attaches policy_fingerprint, a short kms_key_meta (provider:aws|gcp|azure, region, key_hash), and a canonical request-id -> hashed operator mapping for privacy-preserving operator attribution. - Enforce on-accept path: when enforcement mode is enabled, the authorizer rejects a decision if the runtime policy fingerprint does not match the bundle fingerprint declared by the control plane (prevents silent drift from out-of-band changes). - Migrations: backfill script to compute fingerprints for historical policy bundles and re-run canonicalizer over the last 30d of audit events to produce enriched records in the audit-s3/forwarder path (non-destructive). - Feature flag gating and staged rollout: default is "report-only" with a canary group (5% tenants) for enforcement. Ops runbook and console indicators added to track enforcement rejections. Checklist: - [x] fingerprinter implementation + unit tests - [x] runtime authorizer integration + integration tests - [x] audit canonicalizer service + e2e test harness - [x] backfill script + dry-run mode - [x] console UI badge + docs - [x] CI gating job to prevent accidental fingerprint regeneration - [x] rollout plan and runbook attached to Linear tickets
commits: 3 commits: 1) add canonical policy serializer and fingerprint generator (rbac/policy/fingerprint.go), 2) authorizer integration and decision trace propagation (authorizer/trace.go), 3) audit canonicalizer service, backfill script and docs; commit messages include test coverage notes and CI workflow additions.
review_conversation:
Marco: Can you explain collision surface and why SHA-256+B64 is sufficient?
Priya: SHA-256 with canonical JSON normalization is our threat model; collisions are considered infeasible for our retention and audit window. We also include a 6-char human-readable short-id for quick lookups.
Anya: Is there an operator privacy concern with attaching policy fingerprints to decision traces?
Priya: We only include the policy fingerprint and a hashed operator id (HMAC with a per-tenant salt stored in the secrets store) to allow attribution without leaking raw operator identifiers. See audit canonicalizer docs for the privacy design.
Samir: Rollout: how do we handle mismatch spikes during canary?
Priya: We start in report-only mode for 7 days and surface mismatch metrics to console + alert to sec-oncall if mismatch rate > 0.5% for canary tenants. Enforcement can be toggled per-namespace via feature flag.
Anya: CI check to prevent accidental fingerprint churn looks good; please add a clear error message.
Priya: Added better error message and a link to docs in the CI job.
Marco: LGTM after two small nits (naming + comment); approved.
Merge: squash and merge after green CI.
ci_summary: Pipeline: lint -> unit -> integration -> e2e -> build artifacts. First run: lint fail (policy-naming), fix pushed. Second run: all green. Integration tests include decision trace roundtrip and canonicalizer end-to-end with a mocked kms metadata provider. Artifacts: audit canonicalizer image pushed to staging registry.
release_notes: Add deterministic RBAC V2 policy fingerprints and an audit canonicalizer which enriches audit events with policy_fingerprint and compact KMS metadata. Backfill tool provided to reprocess recent audit events. Default: report-only; enforcement can be enabled via feature flag.
merge_outcome: Merged into main. Rollout: report-only enabled globally; enforcement enabled for canary tenants. Backfill job scheduled under maintenance window. Monitoring dashboards and alerts added to Redwood Console and PagerDuty for SEC oncall.
